docs.title: Publish pytest results to Jira and Xray.
docs.text:
Map pytest tests to Jira Test issues. Run your parametrized suite and import aggregate results into an Xray Test Execution, with case details in comments when you enable them.

Start the integration guide Configure authentication

Jira with Xray required · Python 3.12+ · pytest 9.1.1–9.x

docs.title: Connect your tests to your Jira workflow
docs.text:
You need Jira with the Xray app, existing Test and Test Execution issues, and credentials with permission to import results. The requested target is on-premises Xray 8.5.3-j10, targeting existing Generic Tests. Generic is the confirmed Test type; live import behavior on this exact server/version still requires validation. Native iteration rows and datasets are not implemented.

The guide takes you through installation, a marked parametrized test, an Xray payload preview, authentication and import. You then inspect the Test Run in Jira.

  • Map and publish results

    Associate cases with an existing Jira Test and target an existing Test Execution. Preview the payload, then send it using protected environment variables.

    Follow the integration tutorial →

  • Configure your integration

    Find Server/Data Center authentication, execution settings, status rules and exact compatibility limits before applying the exporter to your project.

    Open the reference →

  • Debug and audit an import

    Inspect Xray JSON before sending, retain structured pytest cases and archive full comments. These facilities support the Jira/Xray integration.

    Inspect the import preview →

docs.title: What reaches Jira/Xray?
docs.text:
One aggregate Test Run per Jira Test key, with opt-in case details in its comment. Native Xray iteration rows and datasets are not supported. The local audit report preserves individual pytest cases, but it is not an Xray import format.

Offline previews deliberately make no network request. They help review data; they do not establish valid credentials, permissions, issue keys or server mapping.

Read the compatibility boundaries.

docs.title: Complete documentation
docs.text: The full guide is preserved in the repository README and packaged for PyPI. Website tutorial and reference pages use that same source.

docs.title: Advanced: customize the export with hooks
docs.text:
A hook is a Python function pytest calls at a particular point in a run. You do not need one for the tutorial. If you need custom execution metadata or evidence, create conftest.py beside test_example.py:

import pytest
from pytest_xray import evidence


def pytest_xray_results(results, session):
    results["info"]["revision"] = "tutorial-revision"


@pytest.hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_makereport(item, call):
    outcome = yield
    report = outcome.get_result()
    if report.when == "call":
        report.evidences = getattr(report, "evidences", []) + [
            evidence.text(data="synthetic evidence", filename="example.txt")
        ]

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --jira-xray --xraypath=xray.json --allow-duplicate-ids --xray-parameter-details

Expected: 2 passed. xray.json contains info.revision: "tutorial-revision" and two evidence entries, one per case, on the combined Test result. The evidence text is encoded in the payload. These are Test Run attachments, not per-iteration attachments. cases.json is not written by this command.

When a case maps to multiple Jira Test keys, each key keeps its own evidence and defect lists. For example, case 1 mapped to SYN-1 and SYN-2 with BUG-1, followed by case 2 mapped only to SYN-1 with BUG-2, gives SYN-1 both cases' attachments and defects; SYN-2 receives only case 1's. Two parameter cases both mapped to both keys produce two attachment occurrences per key, even when their filenames and contents are identical. Defect identifiers are still de-duplicated per key.

Version 0.1.4 fixes list sharing that could leak later attachments/defects into an unrelated key or inflate attachment counts. It changes neither status precedence nor comments, and needs no new flags. Use --allow-duplicate-ids when multiple cases reuse a key. The fix applies to serial and xdist file exports and the same payload used for upload; live server behavior has not been revalidated.

pytest_xray_results edits the final legacy payload before archival and comment bounds are applied. The report hook attaches evidence after pytest creates each call report. Hooks execute trusted local Python and can change correctness or expose data; use only the fields and content you intend to export. Delete this optional conftest.py when finished with the example.

docs.title: Associate one function with multiple Tests
docs.text:
Use the passing example from the tutorial.

Replace the marker in step 3 with @pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1", "DEMO-2"). Each marked Test receives the combined result. Use this only when those Test issues are genuinely intended to share the result.

docs.title: Parallel tests and retries
docs.text:
Use the passing example from the tutorial.

Install the optional plugins separately:

python -m pip install pytest-xdist==3.8.0 pytest-rerunfailures==16.7

python -m pytest -q test_example.py -n 2 --xray-case-report=cases.json

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --reruns=1 --xray-case-report=cases.json

-n 2 uses two worker processes. --reruns=1 allows one retry after a failure. Our restored passing example has nothing to retry. With a failing-then-passing test, pytest may exit 0 while this reporter still records an earlier failure; see the status table below. The main process writes one report. Results can arrive in a different order. With --dist=each, the same node observed on two workers is retained as two worker attempts.

docs.title: 0.1.0a2 (2026-10-15)
docs.text:
• Bound HTTP connect/read waits; validate authentication and import responses.
  • Surface publishing failure with a nonzero exit; withhold incomplete remote imports.
  • Preserve failed retry phases in legacy aggregation and write local exports atomically.
  • Add failure, retry and worker regression coverage, installed-wheel CI checks, and complete beginner usage documentation for the PyPI long description.

  • Keep native iterations unimplemented and stable publication blocked on target validation.

docs.title: Project and development
docs.text:
This is an independent Apache-2.0 fork of pytest-jira-xray, based on 6ac1117585da590001cdbc2bf261b78683c19dcb (upstream's 0.9.4 line). Report issues with synthetic examples through GitHub issues.

From a checkout in a fresh environment:

python -m pip install -e . -r requirements-tests.txt build==1.6.1 setuptools==84.0.0 wheel==0.48.0 twine==7.0.0
python -m pytest -q
python tools/reproduce.py src --details
python tools/validate_offline.py
python tools/build_release.py release-dist
python -m twine check release-dist/*

Tests use synthetic data, blocked transport or a localhost fake service. Release evidence distinguishes independent checks from user-reported validation. The sandbox capability procedure is optional research, not implemented native support. It requests no private data. Publishing uses the existing manual workflow, reviewed commit and artifact hashes.

Version tagging adds vX.Y.Z and a matching GitHub Release after a verified PyPI publication, with the exact published wheel and source archive. The approved workflow is enabled; the 0.1.5 backfill and no-op retry were verified. Maintainers: see tagged release setup and retry instructions. Package installation and Jira/Xray configuration are unchanged.

The coverage badge is a measured snapshot of plugin executable lines in src/pytest_xray, from the full synthetic test suite including Python subprocesses. Its linked report identifies the exact commit, measurement time and line/branch counts; it can lag main and is not a live Xray compatibility claim. Tests and repository tools are outside this denominator. Python badges describe the tested 3.12–3.14 matrix; installation requires Python 3.12+. See coverage scope and report updates.

Version, tested Python and licence images are first-party metadata snapshots, refreshed after releases. The test and documentation images show live main-branch workflow status.

docs.title: Maintaining this documentation site
docs.text: The website uses Material for MkDocs, with original project colors and artwork. Tutorial, how-to and reference pages are generated from the tested README. The full PyPI README remains intact; do not edit generated .docs-source files.

docs.title: Build and preview
docs.text:
From the repository root in a development environment:

python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
python tools/prepare_docs_site.py
python -m mkdocs build --strict
python tools/check_docs_links.py
python -m mkdocs serve

Open the localhost URL printed by MkDocs. No credentials are needed. The static output is in site/; its links work under the repository's GitHub Pages path. The browser check in tools/check_docs_browser.py also exercises desktop/mobile navigation, local search, clipboard copying and theme switching against a local server:

python -m pip install playwright==1.64.0
python -m playwright install chromium
python tools/check_docs_browser.py

Set CHROMIUM_PATH if using a system Chromium installation. Screenshots are saved to /tmp/xray-site-preview by default; set DOCS_SCREENSHOTS to choose another path. The existing package CI separately executes the README commands against an installed wheel on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.

docs.title: Publishing model
docs.text:
CI only builds, validates and uploads a reviewable site artifact using repository read permissions. It does not grant itself Pages deployment or identity-token permissions. After review, publish the verified static files on gh-pages using existing repository write access. Pages serves the root of that branch; .nojekyll keeps the static files intact.

The public site is configured to deploy from gh-pages, at /(root). Publication uses the maintainer's existing repository access; no custom domain, extra token, or new publishing credential is required. CI does not publish automatically.

docs.title: Deploy manually from main
docs.text:
Use a clean checkout with existing push access. Start with the reviewed source:

git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
python tools/prepare_docs_site.py
python -m mkdocs build --strict
python tools/check_docs_links.py

Run the browser check above and confirm the checks for this commit have passed. Then fetch the published branch so its history is preserved, and push the built site (ghp_import is installed with MkDocs):

git fetch origin gh-pages:gh-pages
python -m ghp_import -n -p -b gh-pages -m "Publish reviewed documentation from main" site

A non-fast-forward rejection means the local deployment branch is stale; fetch and review the remote state before trying again. Do not force-push. GitHub's built-in Pages build serves the static files, including .nojekyll. Check the Pages deployment runs and open the live tutorial and search before considering publication complete.

For a new repository, pushing its first gh-pages branch may automatically enable Pages. Treat that push as publication and obtain the repository owner's publication authorization first. This repository's public Pages publication is authorized.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Material and MkDocs versions are pinned in requirements-docs.txt. Material's maintainers currently list May 5, 2027 as its end-of-life date; review their maintenance and migration guidance before then. Content stays in ordinary Markdown for a straightforward migration.

docs.title: Result rules and compatibility
docs.text:
Event Local case summary Legacy Xray summary Passing call passed PASS Failed call or fixture setup/teardown failed FAIL Skip skipped ABORTED Expected failure (xfail) skipped; xfail recorded FAIL Unexpected pass (xpass) passed; xpass recorded PASS Strict unexpected pass failed FAIL Failed attempt then successful retry failed; both attempts retained FAIL

The local report preserves any earlier failure. Legacy grouping retains upstream's priority: ABORTED outranks FAIL. A group containing a skip and failure therefore has ABORTED status, with failure information in comments. This differs from local failure-first grouping. Statuses are not interchangeable with pytest's exit code.

Publishing failure changes an otherwise successful pytest exit to 3; an existing nonzero exit is preserved. Remote imports are withheld after worker crashes, fail-fast/maxfail stops, collection failures (including continue-on-error), interruptions, or when there are no marked results. Local files can still contain partial observations. Reports list observed results, not an inventory of tests that never ran. Hard process termination can prevent any final file from being written.

Requests use a 10-second connect timeout and a 60-second read-inactivity timeout, not a total deadline. Redirects are rejected. Authentication and response shapes are checked. The plugin does not dump raw server responses to shared temporary files. Local file replacement is atomic; failed writes retain any prior report.

Python metadata requires >=3.12, pytest >=9.1.1,<10 and requests >=2.34.2,<3. CI checks Linux on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14; the tested baseline uses pytest 9.1.1, requests 2.34.2, xdist 3.8.0 and rerunfailures 16.7. Windows/macOS instructions are provided but those platforms have not been executed in this validation. Future dependency versions are not automatically certified.

Subtests and repeat plugins are not supported as distinct case models. Reliable case identity across worker crashes/restarts, cross-session aggregation and per-iteration evidence are outside this release. Crashed-worker reports can lack parameter metadata or Jira keys. Native rows and datasets are unsupported for the confirmed Generic target.

docs.title: All package options
docs.text:
All on/off switches below default to off. Paths and issue keys are text values and default to unset; --xray-comment-limit is an integer defaulting to 32000. The table describes the combinations required to make each option useful.

Option Effect --xray-case-report=PATH Write observed cases locally. Parent folder must exist. Audit/debug output; does not upload. --xray-case-values Include scalar input values in the case report; requires its path. --xray-case-redact-identities Replace local names/IDs with per-run aliases; requires the case report and excludes case values. --jira-xray Enable export of marked tests. Uploads unless --xraypath is set. --xraypath=PATH With --jira-xray, write Xray JSON instead of uploading. Creates parent folders. --allow-duplicate-ids Combine cases that share a Jira Test key. --xray-parameter-details Add parameter identities and scalar values to legacy comments. --xray-comment-limit=BYTES Maximum UTF-8 bytes per final comment; default 32000, minimum 256. --xray-full-report=PATH Archive the complete original legacy payload before shortening comments; requires --jira-xray. --execution=KEY Update an existing Test Execution. --testplan=KEY Set a Test Plan key in execution metadata. --api-key-auth Authenticate using XRAY_API_KEY as a Bearer token. --client-secret-auth Authenticate with Xray Cloud client credentials. --cloud Use the Cloud import endpoint and status spelling. --add-captures Add captured stdout, stderr and logs to comments; may expose secrets.

Use python -m pytest --help for pytest's own options. --collect-only does not write reports. No option enables native iteration rows.

docs.title: Jira/Xray prerequisites
docs.text:
• A Jira Server/Data Center instance with the Xray app and permission to import test results. The requested target is Xray 8.5.3-j10; this exact server/version has not been independently validated. The implemented transport uses Xray's Server/DC /rest/raven/2.0/import/execution API. Keep --cloud off for this target.
  • An existing Generic Test issue and Test Execution in an authorized project. This guide uses DEMO-1 and DEMO-100 as placeholders; replace them with your own keys before uploading. A Test identifies what is tested; the Execution holds its result. Both input cases share the Test key and produce one Test Run.
  • Generic is the confirmed target Xray Test type. Use an existing Generic Test; the plugin imports results by issue key and does not create, select or change the Test type. This confirmation does not establish native iteration support.
  • An existing Jira personal access token (or administrator-enabled Basic auth), the Jira base URL including any context path, and a trusted TLS certificate/CA. Step 4 configures these through environment variables; never put secrets in tests.
  • Python 3.12+ and pytest 9.1.1–9.x. Use a fresh environment containing this fork only; upstream pytest-jira-xray installs the same module and plugin name.

Use an authorized disposable Test Execution for first validation. Confirm its aggregate result and comments in Jira before using this configuration in production. The preview commands deliberately perform no network requests and do not validate credentials, issue existence, permissions or server-side import behavior.

docs.title: Local JSON report schema
docs.text:
This report helps investigate the individual pytest cases behind aggregate Jira Test Run results. It is an audit/debugging facility within the integration.

pytest --xray-case-report=cases.json writes a local JSON report without requiring Jira markers, credentials, --jira-xray, or duplicate-ID overrides. It has no transport. Do not submit this schema to Xray's import endpoint.

The model in case_results.py depends only on Python's standard library. case_report.py adapts pytest reports to it and writes once on the controller at session end. The report preserves each executed node ID as a distinct case, pytest's effective parameter ID (callspec.id), and all observed attempts. User-supplied IDs are retained as pytest resolves them; duplicate IDs receive pytest's suffixes. Non-parametrized tests have parameter_id: null.

Each attempt stores its reporting worker and an ordered phase list. Each phase has phase, normalized outcome, raw pytest_outcome, and duration in seconds. The adapter snapshots the original outcome before rerunfailures changes its raw report outcome to rerun. Thus a retry retains outcome: failed or error with pytest_outcome: rerun, rather than replacing it with the eventual pass.

docs.title: Parameter privacy
docs.text: Parameter values are absent by default. --xray-case-values separately opts into scalar values: string, boolean, integer, finite float and null. Other values get a placeholder; objects are not repr'd and containers are not traversed. No assertion text, traceback, capture, skip reason or xfail reason is stored. However, pytest node IDs/parameter IDs may themselves contain values; choose safe explicit IDs. This report is not a redaction guarantee. The older --xray-parameter-details comment fallback is a separate opt-in that includes scalar values; enabling a case report does not enable that fallback.

docs.title: Optional redacted identities
docs.text: --xray-case-redact-identities replaces node IDs with case-1, case-2, etc., and parameter IDs with corresponding opaque aliases in this offline file. The controller assigns aliases, so retry grouping and worker ownership survive. Aliases are local to one run, follow arrival order, and cannot be used to match cases across runs. Original IDs are not included in this file. Combining this mode with --xray-case-values is rejected to avoid accidentally reintroducing values. Original identities still exist inside pytest, worker communication, console output, other reporters and any separately enabled Xray comment output. This option redacts only the offline case report, not the entire test process. Two-worker and local failed-then-passed reruns exercise this mode in tests.

docs.title: Aggregation rules
docs.text:
• Every received phase is appended. A setup phase starts an attempt; teardown closes it. A phase without a current attempt starts an incomplete observation. Grouping uses (nodeid, worker_id) so workers cannot overwrite one another.
  • Attempt numbers are local to a case, in controller observation order. They are not globally stable execution IDs or cross-session retry identifiers.
  • Failed call, setup/teardown error, strict XPASS, or an otherwise unclassified rerun makes an attempt failed. Failure takes priority over skips and passes.
  • Skip and XFAIL summarize as skipped; non-strict XPASS summarizes as passed. Their exact normalized outcomes remain available in phase records. Strict XPASS is recognized from pytest's standard [XPASS(strict)] representation; a nonstandard failure representation remains a failure, not a pass.
  • A passing call requires a teardown observation for a complete passed attempt. Unknown phase outcomes or unfinished non-failing attempts are incomplete.
  • Across attempts: failed > incomplete > skipped > passed. A failure followed by a successful retry therefore remains failed in the case summary. The separate pytest_exit_status records pytest's actual session result, which may be zero after successful reruns. This summary does not alter pytest's exit code; report-write failure does (INTERNAL_ERROR).

Cases are sorted by node ID. Attempts/phases retain arrival order. With xdist, arrival order across workers may vary. Output uses a temporary file and atomic replacement; an unwritable destination is reported and exits nonzero. Parent directories must exist. A previous complete file can remain after a write failure: callers must check exit status. Reusing a path replaces the previous session report, not appends to it; choose separate paths for separate runs.

docs.title: Exercised scope and limits
docs.text:
Tested on Python 3.12, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-xdist 3.8.0 and pytest-rerunfailures 16.7: ordinary execution, two-worker load scheduling, --dist=each with the same node on both workers, failed-call reruns locally and with two workers, and a setup-failure rerun locally. Tests cover phase errors, skip/XFAIL/XPASS, duplicate parameter IDs, sensitive-value exclusion, write errors and simultaneous legacy Xray JSON output.

This is not a claim of compatibility with every plugin/version or scheduler. Worker crashes/restarts, teardown-failure reruns, pytest-repeat, subtests, arbitrary third-party retry plugins, and hard process kills are not exercised. Only received test reports are represented: deselected/unexecuted cases, collection errors and worker crashes do not gain fabricated case results. Session exit status remains essential when interpreting partial output. The adapter does not change the inherited legacy Xray publisher's rerun or status semantics. No native Xray reporting is implied by these offline tests.

docs.title: Authentication and execution settings
docs.text:
Choose one authentication method:

Method CLI option Required environment variables Jira personal access token --api-key-auth XRAY_API_BASE_URL, XRAY_API_KEY Basic authentication, if enabled by your administrator Neither auth flag XRAY_API_BASE_URL, XRAY_API_USER, XRAY_API_PASSWORD Xray Cloud client credentials --cloud --client-secret-auth XRAY_API_BASE_URL, XRAY_CLIENT_ID, XRAY_CLIENT_SECRET

Cloud is a different service. It uses the Xray API base URL, /api/v2/authenticate and /api/v2/import/execution, with PASSED/FAILED status spelling. Server/DC uses PASS/FAIL. --cloud does not enable native iterations or change Test types. Cloud has synthetic test coverage, not live target validation.

TLS certificate verification is enabled by default. Set XRAY_API_VERIFY_SSL to True or to a trusted CA bundle path for an internal CA. False disables verification and should not be used with real credentials.

Optional execution metadata:

Environment variable Meaning XRAY_EXECUTION_SUMMARY Execution title. A new execution defaults to Execution of automated tests. XRAY_EXECUTION_DESC Execution description. XRAY_EXECUTION_REVISION Revision, such as a commit ID. XRAY_EXECUTION_TEST_ENVIRONMENTS Environment names separated by whitespace. XRAY_EXECUTION_FIX_VERSION Fix version; the first nonempty parsed value is used.

These variables configure the legacy exporter; local case reporting does not need them. Secrets belong in your shell environment or protected CI settings, not test files or command-line arguments.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and migration
docs.text:
Invalid defects marker (0.1.5+): when --jira-xray is enabled, defects must be a list of nonempty strings. For example, change the marker on your test to:

@pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1", defects=["BUG-1", "BUG-2"])

Use defects=[] or omit it when there are no defects. Do not pass a bare string (defects="BUG-1"), tuple, None, numbers, empty strings or whitespace-only strings. Values are not trimmed or checked against a Jira-key regex; Jira/Xray still determines whether a supplied key exists and is usable.

Run the same offline preview command from the tutorial. Malformed defects now produce a collection error before any test fixtures run, in serial and xdist. Uploads are withheld, even with --continue-on-collection-errors; a local preview may contain an empty tests list for diagnosis. The error describes the required shape without displaying defect values. Fix the marker and rerun. Ordinary pytest runs and local-case reporting without --jira-xray do not apply this validation. --collect-only retains its existing behavior of not configuring Xray reporting; it lists tests but does not validate these markers, run fixtures or upload. This validates marker configuration only; it does not contact Jira or validate credentials. Earlier versions could fail later inside report hooks or retain invalid values in export payloads.

What happened What to do unrecognized arguments Activate the intended environment and use python -m pytest. Check python -m pip show pytest-jira-xray-plus. If plugin autoload is disabled, add -p pytest_xray.plugin. Duplicate plugin/import errors Create a fresh environment with this fork only, not upstream pytest-jira-xray. Duplicate Jira IDs Add --allow-duplicate-ids only when the cases intentionally share one Test. No xray.json Use both --jira-xray and --xraypath=xray.json. Case reporting is separate. Cannot write a report Check permissions and distinct paths. Create the case-report parent folder. A previous file retained after failure is not a new result. Comment exceeds the limit Add --xray-full-report=PATH to retain full text before truncation; inspect the resulting export. Missing authentication variable Set the variables for your selected auth method. Offline file exports do not need credentials. HTTP 401/403 Check existing credentials and permissions with the sandbox administrator. Do not paste secrets into issue reports. HTTP 404 or redirect Check the base URL, context path and Server/DC versus Cloud mode. Certificate error Configure the trusted CA bundle; do not bypass verification. Timeout, invalid JSON or missing execution ID Inspect local server/proxy information and check whether the import already succeeded before retrying. No native parameter rows Expected: this exporter provides aggregate status and optional comment detail, not native iterations.

From upstream: create a fresh environment and install pytest-jira-xray-plus. The Python imports, marker and xray plugin name are retained. Check the dependency requirements, add local reporting as needed, and compare an offline export before uploading. Do not install both distributions together.

From 0.1.0–0.1.2: 0.1.3 confirms Generic as the target Test type in the documentation; runtime behavior is unchanged. From 0.1.0a1: later releases add bounded comments, meaningful publishing failures, atomic file export and failure-preserving rerun summaries; update CI expectations.

docs.title: Integrate pytest with Jira and Xray
docs.text:
Begin with the Jira/Xray prerequisites: your server, existing Generic Test and Test Execution issues, and existing credentials. Install the plugin, map your test, preview the payload, then authenticate and import results. Debugging and audit recipes follow the core integration workflow.

  • 1. Create a project
  • 2. Run two input cases
  • 3. Preview the Jira/Xray import
  • 4. Authenticate and publish to Jira/Xray
  • 5. Audit cases behind a Jira Test Run
  • 6. Choose audit report contents
  • 7. Diagnose a failing case
  • 8. Archive complete Xray comments

Preview commands do not contact Jira. CI executes these commands against an installed package with HTTP blocked; live imports require your authorized Jira/Xray environment. Generic is the confirmed Test type. Live import behavior on Xray 8.5.3-j10 remains unverified; native iteration rows and datasets are not implemented.

docs.title: 8. Archive complete Xray comments
docs.text:
Continue from 7. Diagnose a failing case. Use the same xray-demo folder and activated environment.

Restore the passing, marked test before trying this archive recipe:

import pytest


@pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1")
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value, expected",
    [(1, 2), (2, 3)],
    ids=["one-plus-one", "two-plus-one"],
)
def test_add_one(value, expected):
    assert value + 1 == expected

Large parametrized suites can produce long comments. The default client policy limits each exported comment to 32,000 UTF-8 bytes. This is a configurable client choice, not a universal Jira/Xray server limit.

To see the behavior with our small example, deliberately choose a tiny limit:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --xray-case-report=cases.json --jira-xray --xraypath=xray.json --allow-duplicate-ids --xray-parameter-details --xray-comment-limit=256 --xray-full-report=full-xray.json

Two new options work together:

  • --xray-comment-limit=256 bounds each final exported comment to 256 UTF-8 bytes, including the truncation notice. It does not limit the entire request or attached evidence. The minimum is 256.
  • --xray-full-report=full-xray.json saves the complete original Xray payload before any comment is shortened.

Expected: 2 passed and a message containing truncated 1 comment(s).

File Result cases.json Both structured cases, unaffected by the comment limit. full-xray.json Full original comment containing both case identities and values. xray.json Shortened comment with an explicit TRUNCATED notice.

If an oversized comment has no full-report path, export stops instead of silently losing text. If the archive cannot be written, export also stops. An otherwise passing pytest session then exits with code 3. Statuses and evidence are not truncated. Use the default limit for ordinary evaluation, then validate the appropriate size with your server administrator.

The full archive can contain values, failure text and evidence. Protect it like test data. All three report paths must differ. Files are replaced on each run; choose unique paths to retain history.

docs.title: 2. Run two input cases
docs.text:
Continue from 1. Create a project. Use the same xray-demo folder and activated environment.

Map the example to your Jira Test (DEMO-1 is a placeholder). Create test_example.py inside xray-demo, next to .venv. Paste this complete file:

import pytest


@pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1")
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value, expected",
    [(1, 2), (2, 3)],
    ids=["one-plus-one", "two-plus-one"],
)
def test_add_one(value, expected):
    assert value + 1 == expected

Run it from xray-demo:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py

Expected summary (timing and progress characters may vary):

2 passed

Here is how the file works:

  • import pytest lets us use pytest's test decorators.
  • The function name starts with test_, so pytest discovers it.
  • @pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1") maps both cases to the existing Jira Test.
  • parametrize runs the function once for each input pair: first 1, 2, then 2, 3. These two runs are called cases.
  • ids gives those cases readable names. Use names without secrets.
  • assert checks that adding one gives the expected result.

python -m pytest uses pytest from your active environment. -q keeps output short. This first command checks the test itself. The Jira marker is in place, but uploading starts only when --jira-xray is enabled without --xraypath.

Your folder contains:

xray-demo/
  .venv/
  test_example.py

Pytest may also create cache folders. You do not need to edit them.

docs.title: 7. Diagnose a failing case
docs.text:
Continue from 6. Choose audit report contents. Use the same xray-demo folder and activated environment.

Replace the file with this version. Only the second expected value has changed, from 3 to 99:

import pytest


@pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1")
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value, expected",
    [(1, 2), (2, 99)],
    ids=["one-plus-one", "two-plus-one"],
)
def test_add_one(value, expected):
    assert value + 1 == expected

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --xray-case-report=cases.json

Expected summary:

1 failed, 1 passed

This is an intentional failure. Pytest exits with code 1, rather than 0 for success. The report is still written. one-plus-one remains passed; two-plus-one is failed. Neither case disappears because another case has a different result.

Checkpoint: the audit report retains both input cases behind the Jira Test. This diagnostic run has not updated Jira. Restore passing inputs before the next recipe, and repeat the preview/upload workflow when you intend to update Xray.

docs.title: 1. Create a project
docs.text:
First confirm the Jira/Xray prerequisites. In a terminal, start in a folder where you keep small Python projects. These commands use Bash on Linux or macOS:

mkdir xray-demo
cd xray-demo
python3.12 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install pytest-jira-xray-plus

Here is what each command does:

  • mkdir creates the project folder; cd enters it.
  • python3.12 -m venv .venv creates an isolated Python environment in .venv.
  • Activating it makes python use that environment.
  • pip install installs this package and its required dependencies, including pytest.

On Windows, create the environment with py -3.12 -m venv .venv. Activate it with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell or .venv\Scripts\activate.bat in Command Prompt. Use the same python -m ... commands for the rest of the integration tutorial.

Use a fresh environment. Do not also install pytest-jira-xray: that upstream package and this fork share the pytest_xray module and xray plugin name. Installing both can overwrite files. If that happened, recreate the environment.

No repository clone or configuration file is needed. Package installation needs internet access; the local test commands below do not contact Jira.

docs.title: 5. Audit cases behind a Jira Test Run
docs.text:
Continue from 4. Authenticate and publish to Jira/Xray. Use the same xray-demo folder and activated environment.

Use cases.json to investigate the pytest cases behind an aggregate Jira Test Run. Keep the same marked test file. To reproduce only the local observations while debugging an integration result, run:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --xray-case-report=cases.json

You still get 2 passed. You also get cases.json in xray-demo. The new option tells this plugin where to write its local report. It does not enable Jira uploading.

Open the file in your editor, or pretty-print it:

python -m json.tool cases.json

Here is an excerpt from the report. It shows the actual case names and summaries; we have left out each case's attempts list to keep this first view short:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "pytest_exit_status": 0,
  "cases": [
    {
      "nodeid": "test_example.py::test_add_one[one-plus-one]",
      "status": "passed"
    },
    {
      "nodeid": "test_example.py::test_add_one[two-plus-one]",
      "status": "passed"
    }
  ]
}

pytest_exit_status: 0 means the test session succeeded. A nodeid identifies the file, function and input case. Each full case record also has an attempts list, with observed phases:

Phase Meaning setup Prepare the test and any fixtures. call Run the test function. teardown Clean up after the test.

A fixture is pytest code that prepares or cleans up a test resource. Our example has no custom fixtures, but pytest still reports these phases.

cases.json is replaced on each run. Use a different filename to keep an older run. Its parent folder must already exist. This file is the plugin's own format; it is not an Xray import file.

docs.title: 4. Authenticate and publish to Jira/Xray
docs.text:
Continue from 3. Preview the Jira/Xray import. Use the same xray-demo folder and activated environment.

Publish the reviewed result into Jira/Xray. This step makes the integration request; the preceding payload preview did not contact the server. Start with an authorized disposable test project and existing credentials; no credentials or private test data need to be shared with the maintainer.

docs.title: Prepare the two issue keys
docs.text:
1. Choose an existing sandbox Jira Generic Test issue. Replace DEMO-1 in the marker with its key.
  2. Choose an existing sandbox Test Execution, for example DEMO-100. You will pass that key as --execution.
  3. Preview the intended upload with the command below. Replace DEMO-100 with your chosen execution key. Keep --xraypath=xray.json: this preview is local.
python -m pytest -q test_example.py --jira-xray --execution=DEMO-100 --allow-duplicate-ids --xray-parameter-details --xray-case-report=cases.json --xray-full-report=full-xray.json --xraypath=xray.json

python -m json.tool xray.json

Expect 2 passed. Check testExecutionKey matches the intended execution, tests[0].testKey matches your Test marker, and comment contains the case details you intend to send. This uses the normal comment limit, not the archive recipe's deliberately small demonstration limit. No credentials are required for this file export.

The two keys are not interchangeable: one identifies the Test; the other selects where its result goes.

docs.title: Configure Server or Data Center authentication
docs.text:
This example uses an existing personal access token and Bash. It reads the token without placing it in shell history:

export XRAY_API_BASE_URL='https://jira.example.invalid'
read -r -s -p 'Existing sandbox Jira token: ' XRAY_API_KEY
printf '\n'
export XRAY_API_KEY

Replace the .invalid URL with the authorized sandbox base URL. Include Jira's context path, if it has one, but do not append a REST endpoint. The plugin adds /rest/raven/2.0/import/execution itself.

XRAY_API_BASE_URL tells the plugin where Jira is. XRAY_API_KEY holds the token; --api-key-auth below selects that authentication method. In CI, inject these through protected environment variables rather than committing them to files.

docs.title: Upload the result
docs.text:
Use the same passing test file. This time remove --xraypath:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --jira-xray --api-key-auth --execution=DEMO-100 --allow-duplicate-ids --xray-parameter-details --xray-case-report=cases.json --xray-full-report=full-xray.json

Replace DEMO-100 with your chosen execution key. The new options select token authentication and an existing Test Execution. Keep --cloud off for Server/Data Center.

On successful import, pytest prints the returned Test Execution ID. In Jira, open that Test Execution and the Test Run for your Test. Expect one aggregate result and comment text with case details, not native per-input iteration rows. The two local report files remain available for inspection.

When finished with this Bash session:

unset XRAY_API_KEY

Omitting --execution asks Xray to create a new Test Execution, subject to its required fields and permissions. Start with an explicit disposable execution so you know what is being updated. Reimports can replace existing Test Run details, including dataset/iteration information; inspect a run before retrying a timeout. Imports are not retried automatically because the server might already have accepted the first request. This replacement behavior is documented in the official Server/DC import API.

This command targets an existing Generic Test using the aggregate comment fallback. It does not set or change the Test type, and Generic targeting does not enable native iteration rows or datasets. See the compatibility section below for the tested versions and limits.

docs.title: 6. Choose audit report contents
docs.text:
Continue from 5. Audit cases behind a Jira Test Run. Use the same xray-demo folder and activated environment.

By default, the report includes readable case IDs but excludes input values and failure text. Keep that default unless your integration audit requires more detail. The next two commands show alternative choices, not options to combine.

To include scalar input values:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --xray-case-report=cases.json --xray-case-values

Expected: 2 passed. Each attempt now has parameter_values, such as {"value": 1, "expected": 2} for the first case. This is useful when the values are safe to store; leave the option off otherwise.

To hide the function and parameter identities instead:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --xray-case-report=cases.json --xray-case-redact-identities

Expected: 2 passed. The case names become aliases such as case-1, and input values remain absent. Aliases are assigned in arrival order and cannot be matched across separate runs. This affects only the local JSON, not console output or future Xray comments. It cannot be combined with --xray-case-values.

The following steps return to the default reporting command, so readable case IDs will be present and values will be absent again.

docs.title: 3. Preview the Jira/Xray import
docs.text:
Continue from 2. Run two input cases. Use the same xray-demo folder and activated environment.

Before importing results, review the Xray payload. Keep the passing test and its Jira Test marker; here is the complete file:

import pytest


@pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1")
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value, expected",
    [(1, 2), (2, 3)],
    ids=["one-plus-one", "two-plus-one"],
)
def test_add_one(value, expected):
    assert value + 1 == expected

The marker, @pytest.mark.xray("DEMO-1"), associates both cases with one Jira Test issue. DEMO-1 is just a placeholder here; offline export does not look it up. A Test Execution is the Jira issue that holds a set of test results. A Test Run is the result of one Test inside that execution.

Generate the Xray preview and a case audit report:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --xray-case-report=cases.json --jira-xray --xraypath=xray.json --allow-duplicate-ids
Addition What it does --jira-xray Enables export of tests carrying the Xray marker. --xraypath=xray.json Writes the export to this file instead of sending it. --allow-duplicate-ids Allows the two cases to share DEMO-1; their Xray results are combined.

Expected: 2 passed, plus a message showing the generated Xray report file. You now have two reports with different purposes:

File What you will find cases.json Two separate pytest cases, each passed. xray.json One Xray result for DEMO-1, with status: "PASS".

Why one Xray result? Both cases refer to the same Jira Test. This exporter combines them under that key. It does not create native Xray iteration rows.

To keep readable input details in that combined result, add one more option:

python -m pytest -q test_example.py --xray-case-report=cases.json --jira-xray --xraypath=xray.json --allow-duplicate-ids --xray-parameter-details

Open xray.json. Its comment now contains both case names, scalar input values, the reported phase and its outcome. Open cases.json: it still has two separate records and still excludes input values by default.

--xray-parameter-details is an explicit opt-in because its comments can contain sensitive values. It adds details only for parametrized tests. Without it, passing cases usually have no comment text; failure details can still appear.

Keep --xraypath in every offline export command. Without it, --jira-xray selects uploading. This also applies when options are inherited from pytest.ini or PYTEST_ADDOPTS.
